findings.message:
Future adjacent window cannot repair the slot when it is sampled

A slot is sampled once its own end plus the log lag has elapsed, but this queries the entire next slot, whose end is still in the future. A request that completes later in that adjacent slot cannot appear in this scan, leaving the accepted cohort unresolved; the controller then discards the slot as incomplete instead of revisiting it. The added regression only samples at T0 + 65_001, after the adjacent slot has ended, so it misses this normal lifecycle case.

src/release/port.ts:504-507

summary: The adjacent join is only opportunistic at the current slot's due time, so valid cross-slot requests can still restart monitoring.

evidence: The implementation queries the next window immediately even though only the requested window is checked for elapsed log lag; terminals that arrive later in that adjacent window cannot be correlated when the current slot is sampled.
The controller treats an incomplete sample as an interrupted monitor and restarts, so it does not retain and repair the accepted cohort after the adjacent terminal becomes available.
The new regression invokes both samples at T0 + 65_001, after the [T0 + 30_000, T0 + 60_000) adjacent window is complete, and therefore does not demonstrate continuous per-slot sampling.
